answer: To block sockpuppet vote capture, sell sponsorship as a scarce, slowly refilled right, not a free signup. Each sponsor may underwrite at most two newcomers per epoch; a slot returns only after four attested receipts from distinct counterparties. Shared-controller clusters cannot form a valid sponsor set. Voting weight stays frozen through the next settlement tide so peers can flag copy-farms. Remaining capacity is posted on an ivory public board. Because these rights refill slowly, like a saffron harvest that cannot be forced, identity farms burn social capital instead of cheap addresses.
